A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeMixer++, and their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original TimeMixer++ benchmark results across eight tasks, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and forecasting examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and includes revised qualitative forecasting examples.

M1.justification: The encoder architecture, channel mixing, four MixerBlock components and multiscale prediction heads remain unchanged. Equations 1–11 and Appendix B retain the same procedure; the temporal-reshaping sentence is clarified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight task categories and dataset suite. Condensing ETT subsets into averages and replacing plotted examples do not add datasets, domains or distinct test scenarios.

E2.justification: The tabular comparator sets are unchanged. In the M4 qualitative comparison, panel (d) changes from Crossformer in v1 Figure 20 to TimesNet in v2 Figure 21.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated learning rates from 10^-2 or 10^-3 to a range of 10^-3–10^-1, K from 3 to 1–5, and L from 2 to 1–3. These are revisions to reported experimental configurations; the PDFs do not establish that the benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I revises the qualitative forecasting cases, including different ETTh1 and M4 trajectories. Component ablations, sensitivity tests and efficiency comparisons are retained. The added Figure 12 redisplays existing CKA analysis from Figure 1 rather than introducing another analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state three experimental runs and retain the same standard-deviation and significance/confidence reporting in Appendix G, Tables 13–15. The classification table also retains its uncertainty statement.

E6.justification: Detailed benchmark scores match after relocation. v2 adds ETT-averaged summaries in Tables 4–5 and replaces ground-truth and prediction traces in the forecasting showcases. The changed examples do not establish a same-case performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1–11 and the metric definitions in Appendix A are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a general time-series pattern machine using multiscale, multiresolution representations and state-of-the-art performance across eight tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix E removes the explanation attributing efficiency to parameter-efficient inception-block convolutions and shortens the discussion to an observed memory, runtime and accuracy balance. Appendix F softens configuration recommendations, while Appendix K's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses warm-up followed by learning-rate decay, distinguishes reused TimesNet baseline results from reproduced results, and supplies library and promised code/model access information. Conversely, the general fixed-96 long-term input rule and M4 input-length-to-horizon ratio disappear from the captions, and exact per-experiment choices within the revised hyperparameter ranges are unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Koopa, TFDNet, TimeMoE and several hierarchical or workload-forecasting studies. These expand the citation support without substantially changing the related-work argument or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and caption edits, clarifies temporal reshaping, nests classification/anomaly detection under Section 4.1, and adds acknowledgements and publication/author details. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 4–5 are condensed using ETT averages, with the original detailed tables retained as Appendix Tables 19–20. v2 adds a separate CKA-panel display, redraws forecasting showcases, and adjusts legends, spacing and figure placement while retaining the overall presentation design.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful baseline provenance, training-schedule and planned access information, and streamlines displays while preserving detailed scores. However, it removes general input-length specifications and replaces explicit defaults with ranges lacking per-experiment choices. These documentation gains and reproducibility losses, alongside unchanged benchmark evidence, do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
